aspect: Conditioning happens whether or not the threat lands
description: Ninety alerts of which two are real still produce ninety adrenal responses. The false alarms are not free; physiologically they cost the same.
energy_note: Paying full price for warnings about nothing.

description: In communities bordering Gaza the shelter window is thirty seconds or less. A population living under that clock was the group the Continuous Traumatic Stress Response scale was built and validated on.
energy_note: Half a minute, repeatedly, for years.

aspect: Clashing instructions from the people issuing them
description: During the 2026 strikes, Iranian, US and Israeli officials gave civilians contradictory directives about whether to stay or leave. Being told two incompatible things by authorities is itself a stressor: it removes the possibility of being correct.
energy_note: No available action is the right one.

aspect: The phone becomes the threat object
description: After the war the notification sound still produces the reaction. People silence their phones permanently, which then costs them work, appointments and relationships.
money_note: Missed work and opportunities from an unmonitored phone.
energy_note: Avoiding the device everyone else lives through.

aspect: SECONDARY - hypervigilance is expensive in ordinary life
description: Sustained threat monitoring consumes the same attention that would go to work, study and other people. The output drop is real and is usually attributed by employers to laziness.
energy_note: Judged for capacity that is already spent.
